hero.title: A plaintext, interpreted language where code and data live in one KV tree.
hero.lead: The program counter is a path. The source is the IR. Every value is plaintext — inspectable with any KV client, resumable after a crash.

features.title: Code is data
features.body: A function is a subtree. Its parameters are reads on the negative axis and writes on the positive one — the same shape as every value in kvspace.
features.code: rwfunc add(a:int64, b:int64) -> (c:int64) { a + b -> c }
features.codeHtml: rwfunc add(a:int64, b:int64) -> (c:int64) { a + b -> c }

features.title: The PC is a path — crash-resumable
features.body: There is no separate call stack. Frame depth is written into the program counter itself, so a restarted process can continue from the same instruction.
features.codeHtml: PC    = "/vthread/<vid>/[1]/[3,0]"            vthread vid, frame 1, instruction 3

features.title: Small core, extensions on top
features.body: The core runtime only executes and branches. Every other opcode is registered at /lib/<opcode> and handed to a runtime that declares it.

features.title: The spec is the source of truth
features.body: Language facts live in the spec, not in this page. {{SPEC_COUNT}} spec chapters define the language; {{TUTORIAL_COUNT}} anchored tutorial cases demonstrate it. Read the specification →

features.title: Byte-identical backends
features.body: One PascalCase C ABI, two implementations chosen by DSN. The same program runs against shared memory, files, or Redis with identical bytes.
features.code:
KVSPACE=shm:///tmp/kvlang.shm ./bin/kvlang tutorial/01-basics/hello.kv   # kvspace-c
KVSPACE=fs:///tmp/kvlang-fs   ./bin/kvlang tutorial/01-basics/hello.kv   # kvspace-durable
features.codeHtml:
KVSPACE=shm:///tmp/kvlang.shm ./bin/kvlang tutorial/01-basics/hello.kv   # kvspace-c
KVSPACE=fs:///tmp/kvlang-fs   ./bin/kvlang tutorial/01-basics/hello.kv   # kvspace-durable

features.title: Built for agents
features.body: Source, values, and compiled forms are all plaintext in the same tree. deepx uses kvlang as its front-end language; byteseek reads and rewrites its own code and state through the same KV reads and writes. Read the use cases →

ecosystem.title: Ecosystem
ecosystem.lead: Three layers, one tree. Each layer is independently replaceable.
ecosystem.alt: kvspace at the bottom, layout in the middle, runtime on top

layers.title: kvspace
layers.body: Addressing and memory. One C ABI; shm and durable backends must match byte for byte.

layers.title: layout
layers.body: The o0 compiler. Parses source and writes the KV tree — no optimization, no IR.

layers.title: runtime
layers.body: Pure interpretation: fetch, decode, execute, route. Extensions live at /lib/<opcode>.

home.featuresLead: A small core with everything else registered at a path.

heroLeads: kvlang is an extension-first language. The core stays small; capabilities arrive as runtime extensions and libs. Multiple runtime extensions execute in the same kvspace — one tree of code, frames, and values, visible to every participant.
A runtime registers its opcodes at /lib/<opcode>; a lib is a set of rwir/rwfunc definitions laid out into the same tree.
The deepx repository holds model definitions rather than a runtime extension, and deepx-design is documentation; neither is listed as a runtime below.

Registration styles differ. runtime-c is the C core; runtime-rs and deepx-cpu-compute embed it and declare a capability set. deepx-cpu-compute additionally writes its signatures to /lib/<opcode> for distributed scheduling. deepx-compute-cuda registers tensor functions through its own TfFactory. The Metal compute/heap/io planes and heap-cuda exchange bare opcodes (add, load, print, save) over a Redis task queue rather than through /lib routing.
All deepx extensions are being migrated to embed the runtime-c core and register through the capability/route contract; until that migration completes, the table records their current mechanisms.

rows.name: runtime-c
rows.notes: The minimal core: fetch, decode, execute, control flow, native dispatch. Runtime extensions embed this core rather than fork it.

rows.name: runtime-rs
rows.notes: The first runtime extension and its first lib. Embeds the C core and adds the stdlib opcodes (kv, xv, time, duration, string); the binary is still named kvlang.

rows.name: runtime-rs
rows.notes: The second lib. An agent harness written in kvlang, running on runtime-rs against the same kvspace.

rows.name: deepx-cpu-compute
rows.notes: The CPU op-plat: tensor kernels over OpenBLAS/Highway/OpenMP. Declares myrwircaps = deepx/miaobyte·* (add, sub, mul, div, …), embeds the C core, and writes signatures to /lib for distributed scheduling.

rows.name: deepx-compute-metal
rows.notes: The Metal op-plat. Runs elementwise/reduce/changeshape kernels on the GPU; bare task opcodes arrive over Redis, not through /lib. Requires Metal (no CUDA).

rows.name: deepx-common-metal
rows.notes: The Metal HAL: device detection and shared Metal context used by the other Metal rows.

rows.name: deepx-heap-metal
rows.notes: The Metal heap-plat: tensor lifetime and shared-memory bookkeeping alongside the Metal compute plane. A Redis-driven service, not a kvlang capability set.

rows.name: deepx-io-metal
rows.notes: The Metal io-plat: load / print / save tasks driven over the Redis queue.

rows.name: deepx-compute-cuda
rows.notes: The CUDA op-plat. Registers deepx/miaobyte·* tensor functions through its own TfFactory; built in a CUDA 12.8 container, CMake targets sm_75.

rows.name: deepx-heap-cuda
rows.notes: The CUDA heap-plat: device/host memory lifecycle and synchronisation. A Redis-driven service, not a kvlang capability set.

rows.name: deepx-cuda-kernelcompiler
rows.notes: The GPU kernel compiler: lowers kvlang tensor ops to TileLang kernels (AOT .so); no opcode registration.

runtimes.footnote: Extensions grow by registration, not by changing the core: new capabilities land under /lib, and any runtime can provide them. Each lib requires the runtime in the same row to run; a lib's opcodes are registered under that runtime's /lib/<opcode>.
